In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this pilot study provides preliminary evidence that BIS neurofeedback training may be a viable approach to help stressed healthcare providers to learn to lower their BIS value, and that this may be associated with improvements in wellbeing.
the results of this pilot investigation provide evidence that brain wave self-regulation can indeed be learned and may be associated with wellbeing.

BIS neurofeedback is feasible, safe, and effective for learning receptive awareness in stressed healthcare providers.
the learning of receptive awareness is a feasible and potentially useful approach for healthcare providers who are stressed.
we found that the learning of brainwave self-regulatory techniques via neurofeedback may be beneficial to the health and well-being of healthcare providers.

the stress levels of the healthcare providers were reduced by 23% in just 4 sessions of BIS training.
the BIS neurofeedback system may be used to learn to self-regulate brainwave patterns, which is associated with wellbeing.
